preview: Mrudul Joshi shares their JPMC interview and Code for Good hackathon experience for the 2023 recruitment cycle, detailing the online coding assessment, HireVue video interview, and tips for success.
content: Mrudul Joshi B.Tech CS INTERVIEW EXPERIENCE On-campus Hiring Every year, JPMC recruits interns and full-time employees on campus through an event called Code for Good, which is a 24-hour hackathon. During this event, teams work together to develop technological solutions for challenges faced by non-profit organizations. Eligibility Criteria: Degrees: B.Tech./B.E./MCA Streams: Computer Science/Information Science/ Information Technology/Data Science/Artificial Intelligence/Big Data/IoT/Electronics/ Electrical/Electronics and Telecommunications etc. Minimum aggregate 7 CGPA [until date of registration] in engineering course Timeline: Registration Process: 10th March to 23rd March Online Coding Test: 10th April Video Interview: Deadline 17th April Code for Good Shortlist announcement: 6th June Code for Good Event: 15th and 16th July Internship Shortlist announcement: 28th August Coding Round (60 minutes) The first stage of the SEP selection process involves an online coding assessment via the HackerRank platform. This test consists of two programming questions, each worth 50 marks, totaling 100 marks overall. You are given 60 minutes to complete the test. Following were the questions I had in the coding round: Counting Bits Link to the problem It was a fairly simple problem (can be classified as a leetcode easy problem). I just used a multiset and with good logic I was able to clear all test cases. Apart from that I don’t remember exactly all the test cases, the last few test cases were a bit tricky but doable with time and some thought. I can’t recall the second question now, but it was a leetcode medium question. I was able to finish both questions in 20-25 minutes each. Video Interview (10 minutes) The next stage in the recruitment procedure involves a video interview facilitated by HireVue. During this HireVue session, you'll be prompted to provide recorded video responses to two interview queries. The question types in these video interviews are fairly conventional, some examples are: "Where do you see your career in a decade?" and "Could you discuss your accomplishments and the insights gained from them? Additionally, share a recent learning-intensive experience." I spoke about my career vision and about a recent hackathon experience in regards to my questions. You can just search about these questions online, they are your very typical HR questions. Note that all questions are the same for everyone attempting the round so you can get to know your questions beforehand and prepare a brief response in advance. Shortlist Results The final list of all shortlisted students came out about a month later from the video interview submission, 10 students were selected for the hack. Code for Good 2023 Hackathon (15th &16th) The hackathon for my batch was conducted online. Pre-Hackathon: Before the hackathon JPMC conducts online bootcamps on the required technologies during the hack like GitHub and their communication channel slack, etc. You’ll be assigned your mentors and teammates 2-3 days before the hack starts. Team assignment is unknown to us so your teammates can be from anywhere in India. Generally a team of 6 members is formed with 2-3 mentors. A day before, our team got in touch with each other on a Whatsapp group and discussed our tech stack along with our strengths and weaknesses. We collectively decided on MERN stack as all of us were web developers. There was also an ice-breaking session for the entire team along with the mentors (which was the first time we met our mentors by the way). During the session, everyone got to know each other well, overall very typical. During Hackathon: The day of the hack started with an introductory session wherein we got to know more about JPMC and the work culture there, what opportunities are available, etc. Basically if you get in, what will you be getting into lol. After the session the NGO coordinators presented their problem statements to the teams and all teams were given some to discuss and decide a preference order for problem statements. A form was released then where we had to submit our preferences and the allocation was done on a first come first serve basis. After you are allocated your problem statement, your team along with all the teams that have the same problem statement will have a separate meeting with the respective NGO coordinator to understand their requirements further in much detail and also ask any questions that you may have. The actual brainstorming and coding starts after this. Throughout the hackathon the mentors were present with us on a zoom call and observed the way we ideated, brainstormed and came up with a solution. Unlike other mentors, our mentors didn’t take any one to one interview/ QnA, they purely judged us based on how we performed individually and as a team (in terms of tech stack and team work). My Tips for CFG: Be a leader. I took charge in my team right from the start, whether it was interacting with my teammates or working as a team alongside our mentors. Just remember to lead while also giving everyone a fair chance to contribute to the team. Be quick in decision making and do not be stuck on a small problem for a large amount of time. It's fine if your teammates aren’t as proficient as you in your chosen tech stack. Many of my teammates only knew basic HTML/CSS. You can always divide the work in a manner that plays with everyone’s strengths. Be confident and out there with your ideas and points. Nobody will know how smart you are if you are not heard. Winning isn't everything, securing an internship through this hackathon is about showcasing your best all-around self. This includes not only technical skills but also your personality, teamwork abilities, and work ethic. We did not win the hackathon, but 4 out of 6 (including me) in our team got an offer a month later from JPMC to join as SEP interns for summer 2024. Internship Offer After 1 month, the internship selections were announced, 6 out of 10 received internship offers, and all 6 accepted the offer since the results were announced before the arrival of any other company in the college. Tips In General 1. Keep practicing DSA questions (450Sheet, Blind 75) from Leetcode, CodeChef or any other platform. 2. Be up to speed on core subjects/concepts like OS, DBMS and OOPS (our curriculum is good enough, else you can also refer to GFG). 3. Make sure that you are confident in your English speaking and presentation skills. 4. It’s fine if you aren’t proficient in the entire tech stack (eg. MERN/MEAN) it’s about how good you are at whatever you do. Apart from this I know this entire process can be very draining and mentally exhausting (trust me we all have been there) so make sure that you keep your health, both mentally and physically in check. Do not decide your self worth based on this. Getting an internship is super cool but your worth is not dependent on just getting an internship in a company. Be happy and enjoy the ride! Good luck. External Links: Link to DSA questions: https://www.techinterviewhandbook.org/grind75 Link to DSA bootcamp/course on Udemy: https://shorturl.at/HKPV9 Link to Practice HireVue questions: https://shorturl.at/bcjsA Slightly long but a great Google Mock Coding Interview: https://shorturl.at/wAMT5 Cheers!
